editor_note: Entry 27 is faithful and reads naturally. The default of 250マイクロ秒 is kept, and the trade-off is rendered correctly and in the right direction: 「`rep_delay` を下げると QPU の総実行時間は短縮されますが、状態準備のエラー率が増加する」.
Entry 4 is faithful. "以下の要件を使用して開発されました" keeps the source meaning, and "これらのバージョン以降を使用することをお勧めします" correctly carries the "these versions or newer" recommendation in plain desu/masu with no keigo.

Both rewritten cards keep their meaning, so neither would mislead a learner, but a native editor would still change a few things. Both end in the honorific 「ご覧ください」, which breaks the page's plain desu/masu convention; the other cards use plain forms such as 「探索します」 and 「試してください」. In entry 12, 「クラスモジュール」 is an unclear calque of "classroom modules" and should be 「授業用モジュール」. In entry 13, 「厳選されたシーケンス」 inside one long pre-nominal clause reads like translationese; 「厳選して体系的にまとめた」 would read more naturally.

examples.source: Explore our free learning offerings, such as full courses and classroom modules.
examples.translation: フルコースやクラスモジュールなど、無料の学習コンテンツをご覧ください。
examples.suggested: フルコースや授業用モジュールなど、無料の学習コンテンツを探索できます。
examples.why: 「ご覧ください」 is honorific, which the register convention rules out. 「クラスモジュール」 is ambiguous: it could be read as a programming 'class module'.

examples.source: Explore curated sequences of learning, documentation, and tutorial content designed to facilitate knowledge and skill-building in specific interest areas.
examples.translation: 特定の関心領域における知識とスキルの習得を促進するために設計された、学習・ドキュメント・チュートリアルコンテンツの厳選されたシーケンスをご覧ください。
examples.suggested: 特定の分野の知識とスキルを身につけられるよう、学習・ドキュメント・チュートリアルのコンテンツを厳選して体系的にまとめた学習パスを探索できます。
examples.why: The long calqued modifier chain and 「厳選されたシーケンス」 read as translationese. 「ご覧ください」 is also an honorific slip.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 18, "`qiskit-ibm-runtime` のインストール", is faithful to its English and uses the same nominalized heading style as entry 5, "新しい仮想環境の作成とアクティブ化".

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. Entry 25 keeps the 28-day rolling window (28 日間のローリング使用ウィンドウ) and the order "pending jobs stay queued, active jobs keep running" (保留中のワークロードは…キューに残りますが…アクティブなワークロードは引き続き実行されます). Entry 26 keeps the "not limited" condition and "are likely to" (可能性が高くなります).

The page is mostly faithful and natural. IDプロバイダー（IDP）, シングルサインオン（SSO） and the link titles are consistent, and the register is plain desu/masu. One problem is in the tip in entry [7]. It renders "when they join" as ユーザーがグループに参加するたびに, which says users are joining a group. The English means users joining the account or organization. The translation also drops "every group", so the point of dynamic rules (automatically assigning new users to groups) comes across less clearly.

examples.source: you can set up dynamic rules so you don't have to manually add every user to every group when they join.
examples.translation: 動的ルールを設定することで、ユーザーがグループに参加するたびに手動で追加する手間を省くことができます。
examples.suggested: 動的ルールを設定すると、新しいユーザーが加わるたびに各ユーザーをすべてのグループへ手動で追加する必要がなくなります。
examples.why: The translation says users join a group, but in the English they join the account and the rule adds them to groups. It also drops 'every group'. This is a slight drift, but the meaning is still recoverable.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. No claim is inverted, dropped or invented, and the register stays plain desu/masu. Two small wording issues remain. In [4], 「活動的で歓迎的なグループ」 is a stiff calque of "dynamic and welcoming group", because 歓迎的 is not natural Japanese. In [6], "participate in the development" becomes 「発展に貢献する」 ("contribute to"), which states the invitation a little more strongly than the English does.

examples.line_approx: Qiskitコミュニティは…活動的で歓迎的なグループです。
examples.source: The Qiskit community is a dynamic and welcoming group of developers, scientists, and enthusiasts
examples.translation: 開発者、科学者、愛好者からなる活動的で歓迎的なグループです。
examples.suggested: 開発者、科学者、愛好家が集う、活気にあふれ誰でも歓迎されるコミュニティです。
examples.why: 歓迎的 is an unnatural word-for-word calque of 'welcoming'. A native technical writer would rephrase it, for example as 誰でも歓迎される or オープンな.

examples.line_approx: Qiskitコミュニティに参加することで、量子技術の発展に貢献することができます。
examples.source: By joining the Qiskit community, you can participate in the development of quantum technologies.
examples.translation: 量子技術の発展に貢献することができます。
examples.suggested: 量子技術の開発に参加することができます。
examples.why: The English says 'participate in the development'. The translation says 'contribute to the advancement', which is a slight shift in wording. It is harmless, but 開発に参加 is closer to the source.

editor_note: In entry 19, "total input and output dimension" becomes 「入力・出力次元の合計」. That reads as the sum of the input and output dimensions, when the English means the overall input dimension and the overall output dimension of the whole system. The tuple `(input_dim, output_dim)` in the very next sentence makes the intended meaning clear, so a learner is unlikely to be misled, but the wording should still be fixed. The entry also renders "underlying matrix" as 「基底となる行列」. In a quantum text, 基底 reads as "basis", so 「内部の行列」 is clearer. The same phrasing appears in entries 17 and 18, which are outside this delta. The note's negation and order ("reverse of the shape" → 「逆順」) are faithful.

examples.source: To return the total input and output dimension of the operator
examples.translation: 演算子の入力・出力次元の合計を返すには
examples.suggested: 演算子全体の入力次元と出力次元を返すには
examples.why: 合計 suggests input+output are summed; the property returns the full-system input and output dimensions as a pair.

examples.source: the reverse of the shape of the underlying matrix
examples.translation: 基底となる行列の形状とは逆順です
examples.suggested: 内部で保持している行列の形状 (shape) とは逆順です
examples.why: 基底 is the standard term for 'basis' in quantum computing, so 基底となる行列 can be misread as a basis matrix.

editor_note: Both rewritten headings mean the right thing and would not mislead a learner. The problem is that they break the page's naming convention. Every other plan heading keeps the IBM product name in Latin script (Open Plan [6], Flex Plan [10], Pay-As-You-Go Plan [15]), and the body text refers to "Premium Plan" in Latin in [13] and [19]. The rewrites switch to katakana, "プレミアム・プラン" [18] and "オンプレミス・プラン" [21], so a reader sees one plan under two names on the same page. Change both headings back to the English product names to match the page.

examples.source: Premium Plan {#premium-plan}
examples.translation: プレミアム・プラン {#premium-plan}
examples.suggested: Premium Plan {#premium-plan}
examples.why: Entries [13] and [19] call this plan "Premium Plan", and the sibling headings keep English plan names. The katakana heading names the same plan differently from the body text.

examples.source: On-Prem Plan {#on-prem-plan}
examples.translation: オンプレミス・プラン {#on-prem-plan}
examples.suggested: On-Prem Plan {#on-prem-plan}
examples.why: Open Plan, Flex Plan and Pay-As-You-Go Plan are all kept in Latin script. Rendering this one product name in katakana doesn't match that convention.

editor_note: Both rewritten headings are faithful, idiomatic, and keep their anchors unchanged. "Options for state-plotting functions" became 状態プロット関数のオプション, which matches the "状態プロット関数" wording used in entry 48, and "Next steps" became the standard 次のステップ.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. Entry 27 renders the appositive with parentheses (「IBM Quantum プリミティブ（EstimatorV2およびSamplerV2）」) and keeps エラー緩和. Entry 34 keeps the hedge 「アクセスしやすくなる場合があります」 and moves "rather than building your own" into its own sentence, 「これらのテクニックを独自に実装する必要はありません」, without changing the meaning.

The translation is faithful and reads naturally. It keeps the deprecation dates and versions exactly (pulse removal in early 2025, v1.3.0 deprecation and v2.0.0 removal), and the terms are used consistently: フラクショナルゲート, 量子ビット, トランスパイルパイプライン, キャリブレーション.

The meaning is faithful throughout, including the caveats in notes 4 to 9 (parse limits as of July 2025, the eager evaluation of gate modifiers, and nested control flow not being eligible for hardware). Nothing here would mislead a learner. There are three small wording problems. In note 5, "strongly discouraged" became 古典レジスタのエイリアシングの使用は強く推奨されません, which can be read as "not strongly recommended" and so sounds weaker than the English; 強く非推奨です or 避けることを強く推奨します would keep the warning at full strength. In note 6, "Circuit boxes" was left as English prose, and the note 5 phrase ハードウェアでの実行にサポートされていません reads stiffly.

examples.line_approx: 5. ... but it is strongly discouraged to use aliasing of classical registers
examples.source: it is strongly discouraged to use aliasing of classical registers
examples.translation: 古典レジスタのエイリアシングの使用は強く推奨されません
examples.suggested: 古典レジスタのエイリアシングの使用は強く非推奨です
examples.why: 「強く推奨されません」 can be parsed as 'not strongly recommended', which is weaker than the English 'strongly discouraged'. 「強く非推奨」 keeps the full strength of the warning.

examples.line_approx: aliased classical registers are not supported for execution on hardware
examples.source: aliased classical registers are not supported for execution on hardware
examples.translation: エイリアスされた古典レジスタはハードウェアでの実行にサポートされていません
examples.suggested: エイリアスされた古典レジスタは、ハードウェア上での実行ではサポートされていません
examples.why: 「実行にサポートされていません」 is a calque of the English and reads stiffly. 「実行ではサポートされていません」 is how a Japanese technical writer would say it.

examples.line_approx: circuit boxes (`QuantumCircuit.box`) can also have explicit durations
examples.source: circuit boxes (`QuantumCircuit.box`) can also have explicit durations
examples.translation: Circuit boxes（`QuantumCircuit.box`）にも明示的な持続時間を設定できます
examples.suggested: 回路のボックス（`QuantumCircuit.box`）にも明示的な持続時間を設定できます
examples.why: The English plural noun phrase was left untranslated in the middle of Japanese prose.

editor_note: Entry 49 is a line of the Ollama Modelfile TEMPLATE, which is code, and the rewrite translated the literal prompt label "Question:" to "質問:". A learner who copies it gets a prompt format that does not match what the Qiskit model expects. It also no longer matches the untranslated "Answer:" in entry 50 or the PARAMETER stop "Question:" in entry 51, so the published configuration silently changes. Entry 49 must keep "Question:" verbatim. Entries 16 and 21 are faithful. Entry 28 is accurate but reads a little stiffly ("Ollama を通じて"), and its spacing around Latin terms differs from entry 65.

examples.source:
{{ end }}{{ if .Prompt }}Question:
{{ .Prompt }}
examples.translation:
{{ end }}{{ if .Prompt }}質問:
{{ .Prompt }}
examples.suggested:
{{ end }}{{ if .Prompt }}Question:
{{ .Prompt }}
examples.why: This is literal Modelfile template text, not prose. Translating it changes the model's prompt format and breaks its match with 'Answer:' (entry 50) and the stop sequence 'Question:' (entry 51), so the configuration a learner copies differs from the official one.

examples.source: Manually deploy the Qiskit Code Assistant models in local through Ollama
examples.translation: Qiskit Code Assistant モデルをローカルで Ollama を通じて手動でデプロイする
examples.suggested: Ollamaを使用してQiskit Code Assistantモデルをローカルで手動デプロイする
examples.why: Accurate but a slightly stiff calque ('through' → 'を通じて'), and it puts spaces around Latin terms where the parallel title in entry 65 does not. Minor only.

editor_note: Entry 7 is faithful, and its plain desu/masu register fits the page. It renders "requirements" as 以下の要件, "these versions or newer" as これらのバージョン以降 (which keeps the "or newer" meaning), and "We recommend" as お勧めします.

Both rewritten entries are faithful. Entry 25 keeps the condition intact (「プリミティブを初期化した後にオプションを設定する場合…インスタンス化する必要はありません」), and entry 18's shorter 「詳細については…を参照してください」 is a defensible compression, since the linked targets are themselves the class names.
The two rewritten link labels are faithful, conventional renderings: 'dynamical decoupling' as ダイナミカル・デカップリング and 'Pauli twirling' as Pauli ツワーリング, with both URLs left unchanged.

The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the get_runtime_service caveat in [30]-[32] and the serializable-input restriction in [27], and core terms stay consistent (トランスパイル, バックエンド, 回路). The problems are all in the phrasing. [27] stacks two causal clauses (「そのため、…できないため、」). [31] translates "bare" literally as 「裸の」. [17] renders "setting up … into a directory" as 「ディレクトリに設定する」 where 「配置する」 is the natural verb. [6] uses the more formal 「ご確認ください」.

examples.source: For this reason, you cannot pass in `backend` directly, so use `backend_name` as a string instead.
examples.translation: そのため、`backend`を直接渡すことはできないため、代わりに文字列として`backend_name`を使用します。
examples.suggested: そのため、`backend`を直接渡すことはできません。代わりに`backend_name`を文字列として渡します。
examples.why: The sentence has two causal clauses in a row (そのため…ため), which reads as machine translation.

examples.source: A bare `QiskitRuntimeService` submits jobs that the platform never associates with your Serverless job
examples.translation: 裸の`QiskitRuntimeService`が送信するジョブは…
examples.suggested: `QiskitRuntimeService`を直接使用して送信したジョブは…
examples.why: 「裸の」 is a literal calque of 'bare'. A Japanese technical writer would describe it as using the class directly.

examples.source: Qiskit Serverless requires setting up your workload’s `.py` files into a dedicated directory.
examples.translation: ワークロードの`.py`ファイルを専用のディレクトリに設定する必要があります。
examples.suggested: ワークロードの`.py`ファイルを専用のディレクトリに配置する必要があります。
examples.why: Files are placed in a directory (配置), not 'set' into one (設定). The current verb is a calque.

examples.source: find release notes and the most recent documentation at the Qiskit Serverless GitHub page.
examples.translation: …リリースノートと最新ドキュメントをご確認ください。
examples.suggested: …リリースノートと最新ドキュメントを確認してください。
examples.why: ご確認ください is more formal than the plain desu/masu register the project uses.

editor_note: Entry 5 is accurate: both the version note and the "these versions or newer" recommendation (これらのバージョン以降を使用することをお勧めします) are kept. The problem is 以下の要件を使用して開発されました, a word-for-word copy of "developed using the following requirements". A native writer would not say 要件を使用して; 以下の環境（パッケージバージョン）で開発されました is the normal way to put it. Outside the scope of this delta: entry 15 does not translate its English ("In the Qiskit SDK, this Hamiltonian could be constructed with the following code") and instead repeats the opening of entry 16. It should get its own fix pass.

examples.source: The code on this page was developed using the following requirements.
examples.translation: このページのコードは、以下の要件を使用して開発されました。
examples.suggested: このページのコードは、以下の環境で開発されました。
examples.why: 要件を使用して開発 copies the English wording word for word. In Japanese you develop code in an environment or with specific versions, so 環境 is the natural noun here.

editor_note: The meaning is accurate throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The plan-specific usage windows are all correct: the rolling 28 days for Premium/Open, since instance creation for Pay-As-You-Go, and since the contract start for Flex. The problem is that UI labels are handled inconsistently. **Billing overview** and **Instance usage** are translated (請求の概要, インスタンスの使用量), but the "Usage" column in [11] stays in English, so a reader can't tell which labels match the on-screen text. There is also a small calque: "full cost and billing details" became 完全なコストおよび請求の詳細.

examples.source: view the "Usage" column for the workload
examples.translation: 対象のワークロードの「Usage」列を確認してください
examples.suggested: Use one convention for UI labels on the whole page: keep all of them in English (as in 「Usage」) or translate all of them (e.g. 「使用量」(Usage) 列).
examples.why: Entries [5] and [6] translate the UI labels Billing overview and Instance usage, but this entry keeps Usage in English, so labels are treated inconsistently on the same page.

examples.source: for full cost and billing details
examples.translation: 完全なコストおよび請求の詳細を確認できます
examples.suggested: コストと請求の詳細をすべて確認できます
examples.why: 完全な is a literal rendering of 'full'. A Japanese technical writer would say 詳細をすべて or just 詳細な.

editor_note: Entry 29, the Credly privacy notice, keeps the full meaning of the English. It includes the data processor authorized by IBM and located in the US, the data shared (name, email address, badge earned), the permissive 「共有する場合があります」 for "may share", and both links, so nothing in it would mislead a reader. There are two wording problems. 「バッジを請求する」 is a literal rendering of "claiming the badge" that reads like asking for payment or making a demand; natural Japanese would be 「バッジを受け取る」. 「グローバルな第三者」 copies the English structure and misreads "globally" as describing the third parties; 「世界各国の第三者」 fixes this.

examples.line_approx: Credlyからバッジを請求するための手順
examples.source: instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: Credlyからバッジを請求するための手順が記載されたメール通知を受け取ります。
examples.suggested: Credlyから、バッジの受け取り方法を記載したメール通知が届きます。
examples.why: 「請求」 suggests billing or a formal demand. Credly and IBM Japan say 「受け取る」 for accepting a badge, and 「通知が届きます」 reads more naturally than 「通知を受け取ります」.

examples.line_approx: IBMの子会社およびグローバルな第三者
examples.source: with IBM subsidiaries and third parties globally
examples.translation: IBMは、収集した個人情報をIBMの子会社およびグローバルな第三者と共有する場合があります。
examples.suggested: IBMは、収集した個人情報を世界各国のIBM子会社および第三者と共有する場合があります。
examples.why: This copies the English structure. "Globally" describes where the information is shared, not what kind of third party it is, and 「グローバルな第三者」 is not natural Japanese.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. Terminology is correct and consistent (量子ビット, 測定, 相関, エンタングルメント, 複合システム), and the polite desu/masu register holds with no keigo. Nothing here would mislead a learner, but two spots read stiffly. In [5], the English relative clause "to which the discussion in the previous lesson applies" became a separate sentence, 前のレッスンの議論はそのまま適用できます, which no longer says that the previous lesson applies because the systems are treated as one compound system. In [6], 選択するかもしれません and the repeated 集合的に are calques of "may … choose to" and "collectively" that a native editor would smooth out.

examples.source: we can always choose to view multiple systems together as if they form a single, compound system — to which the discussion in the previous lesson applies.
examples.translation: それは、複数のシステムを常に*まとめて*一つの複合システムとして捉えることができる、という点です。前のレッスンの議論はそのまま適用できます。
examples.suggested: それは、複数のシステムを常に*まとめて*一つの複合システムとして捉えることができ、その複合システムには前のレッスンの議論がそのまま適用できる、という点です。
examples.why: Splitting the relative clause into its own sentence cuts the link between 'the compound system' and 'the previous lesson applies to it'. The standalone sentence reads as disconnected.

examples.source: we may have multiple quantum systems that are collectively in a particular quantum state, and then choose to measure some but not all of the individual systems.
examples.translation: 複数の量子システムが集合的に特定の量子状態にある場合に、その中の一部のシステムだけを測定することを選択するかもしれません。
examples.suggested: 複数の量子システムが全体としてある特定の量子状態にあるとき、そのうち一部のシステムだけを測定する、という場合があります。
examples.why: 「〜することを選択するかもしれません」 is a literal calque of 'may choose to', and 集合的に is stiff. 全体として / 〜という場合があります reads more natural in Japanese technical prose.

editor_note: The meaning of rewritten entry 16 matches the English: the five-qubit blocks, the depth-one circuit, qubit 0 and qubit 1, and the transversal conclusion all carry over, so a learner would not be misled. There are two wording slips. "topmost qubit" is rendered 最上位の量子ビット, which Japanese readers often read as "most significant" (最上位ビット = MSB). That clashes with the parenthetical 量子ビット0, which is the least significant qubit in Qiskit. 一番上の量子ビット is clearer and matches the next line's 上から2番目. Also, "target" is rendered 標的 here but ターゲット量子ビット in entry 5, so the term is inconsistent within the page.

examples.source: both the control and target for the first CNOT is the topmost qubit (that is, qubit 0 using the Qiskit numbering convention)
examples.translation: 最初のCNOTの制御と標的はどちらも最上位の量子ビット（すなわち、Qiskitの番号付け規則で量子ビット0）であり、
examples.suggested: 最初のCNOTの制御と標的はどちらも一番上の量子ビット（すなわち、Qiskitの番号付け規則で量子ビット0）であり、
examples.why: Readers often take 最上位 to mean 'most significant', but Qiskit's qubit 0 is the least significant qubit. 一番上 means 'drawn at the top', which is what the English says, and it matches the next line's 上から2番目.

examples.source: both the control and target ...
examples.translation: 制御と標的
examples.suggested: 制御とターゲット
examples.why: Entry 5 uses ターゲット量子ビット for 'target', so this page uses two different terms for it. Pick one and use it throughout.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The threshold-theorem claims in [5] and [7] are intact, including the key point that the threshold does not depend on circuit size (規模には*依存しない*), and the terms are used consistently (キュービット, 論理キュービット, しきい値定理, フォールトトレラント, トランスバーサル, マジックステート). Two phrasings are calqued from English and a native editor would change them. In [5], 「これはすべて大きな課題をもたらします」 is a literal rendering of "This all presents a major challenge". In [7], "high-level discussion" becomes 「高レベルな議論」, where 「概要的な議論」 or 「大まかな議論」 would sound natural. Neither would mislead a learner.

examples.source: This all presents a major challenge.
examples.translation: これはすべて大きな課題をもたらします。
examples.suggested: これらはいずれも大きな課題です。
examples.why: This is a word-for-word calque of 'This all presents'. Using 「すべて」 as the subject together with 「もたらす」 sounds like machine translation.

examples.source: the lesson concludes with a high-level discussion of the threshold theorem
examples.translation: レッスンはしきい値定理の高レベルな議論で締めくくります
examples.suggested: 最後に、しきい値定理について概要レベルで議論してレッスンを締めくくります
examples.why: 「高レベルな議論」 is a calque that can read as 'advanced discussion', which is the opposite of the intended meaning of an overview. The inanimate subject 「レッスンは…締めくくります」 is also stiff.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Entry 16 renders "error bound" as 誤り率の上界, matching entry 14, and entry 23 keeps both expectations (a rising threshold and falling physical noise) under 考えるのが妥当です without overstating either. Two small style points: 楽観をもたらしてくれます in entry 23 is a calque of "provide us with optimism", and 楽観的な見通しを与えてくれます would read more naturally. Entry 16 also uses さらに twice in one short sentence (さらにもう一度…さらに小さく).

examples.source: provide us with optimism as we continue to push forward
examples.translation: 前進を続ける私たちに楽観をもたらしてくれます。
examples.suggested: 前進を続ける私たちに楽観的な見通しを与えてくれます。
examples.why: 楽観をもたらす is a word-for-word calque of 'provide optimism'. A Japanese technical writer would say 楽観的な見通し or 希望を与える.

examples.source: Another iteration reduces the error bound further, to
examples.translation: さらにもう一度反復すると、誤り率の上界はさらに小さくなり、次のようになります。
examples.suggested: もう一度反復すると、誤り率の上界はさらに小さくなり、次のようになります。
examples.why: さらに appears twice in one short sentence. Dropping the first one reads more smoothly and keeps the meaning.

editor_note: The translation is accurate and would not mislead a learner. Key terms are rendered consistently: クエリモデル, 定量的な優位性, and 堅牢かつ納得のいく形 for "robust and satisfying". There are two small slips. In the video title [8], the name is written "simonのアルゴリズム" in lowercase, while [5] uses "Simonのアルゴリズム". In [7], two sentences in a row end with "〜こともできます", which reads a little mechanically.

examples.source: These include the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm and Simon's algorithm.
examples.translation: これにはDeutsch-Jozsaアルゴリズムとsimonのアルゴリズムが含まれます。
examples.suggested: これにはDeutsch-JozsaアルゴリズムとSimonのアルゴリズムが含まれます。
examples.why: The proper name is in lowercase, so it doesn't match 'Simonのアルゴリズム' in entry [5].

examples.source: Alternatively, you can open the [YouTube video] ... [Download the slides] for this lesson.
examples.translation: …別ウィンドウで開くこともできます。このレッスンの[スライドをダウンロード]することもできます。
examples.suggested: …別ウィンドウで開くこともできます。このレッスンの[スライド](...)もダウンロードできます。
examples.why: Two sentences in a row end with 'こともできます', which reads like machine translation. Changing the second ending would make it flow more naturally.

editor_note: The meaning is accurate throughout. The 20 questions, the 16-correct pass mark, the lock after two failed attempts and the Credly privacy terms all match the source, so a learner would not be misled. Several entries break the plain desu/masu convention by slipping into keigo: ご協力いただき and 活用させていただきます in [5], ご利用いただけない場合がございます in [10], and ご覧いただけます in [12]. [5] also uses ご協力 twice in one sentence. The course title is left in English in [5] but translated as 量子情報の一般的な定式化 in [1] and [7]. In [12], 米国在住 is used for a company, where 米国に所在する would be the right wording.

examples.source: Please take a moment to help us improve our course by filling out the following quick survey. Your feedback will be used to enhance our content offering...
examples.translation: ぜひ少し時間を取って、次の簡単なアンケートにご協力いただき、私たちのコースの改善にご協力ください。皆様のフィードバックは、…向上に活用させていただきます。
examples.suggested: 少し時間を取って、次の簡単なアンケートに回答し、コースの改善にご協力ください。フィードバックはコンテンツとユーザー体験の向上に活用します。
examples.why: Keigo (いただき／させていただきます) goes against the plain desu/masu convention, and ご協力 appears twice in one sentence.

examples.source: These exams on the IBM Training site may be temporarily unavailable in the next few days, due to maintenance.
examples.translation: …一時的にご利用いただけない場合がございます。
examples.suggested: …一時的に利用できない場合があります。
examples.why: ございます and ご利用いただけない are keigo, which the register convention forbids.

examples.source: the "General formulation of quantum information" course
examples.translation: 「General formulation of quantum information」コース
examples.suggested: 「量子情報の一般的な定式化」コース
examples.why: The course title stays in English here but is translated in [1] and [7], so the file is inconsistent.

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM and located in the United States
examples.translation: IBM が認定した米国在住のサードパーティデータ処理業者
examples.suggested: IBM が認定した、米国に所在するサードパーティのデータ処理業者
examples.why: 在住 is used for people who live somewhere; for a company, 所在 is the natural word.

editor_note: Entry [4] gives the relative clause the wrong subject. The English says the *series* comprises the listed courses. The Japanese, "本コースは、…シリーズの第3コースであり、以下のコースで構成されています", says *this course* is made up of them. The list that follows includes "(本コース)", so readers can recover the right meaning, but the sentence as written is wrong and should be restructured. The rest reads naturally and is faithful: 密度行列, チャネル, 一般的なクラスの測定, and 操作的に for "operational" are all correct.

examples.source: the third course in the *Understanding Quantum Information and Computation* series comprising the following courses:
examples.translation: 本コースは、*量子情報と計算の理解* シリーズの第3コースであり、以下のコースで構成されています。
examples.suggested: 本コースは、以下のコースで構成される *量子情報と計算の理解* シリーズの第3コースです。
examples.why: "comprising" refers to the series, but the Japanese makes 本コース the subject of 構成されています. That says this course is made up of the four listed courses, one of which is this course itself.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful and the prose reads as native Japanese. Terms are consistent, with purification as 精製, fidelity as フィデリティ, dilation as 拡張 and Uhlmann's theorem as ウールマンの定理, and the "provided the traced-out portion is large enough" caveat in [3] is kept.

Nothing here would mislead a learner. The pass mark (16 of 20), the lockout after two failed attempts, the badge being emailed to the IBM Training address and the Credly data-sharing terms all match the English. Entry [10] has a stray character: "これらのAの試験" should read "これらの試験". Entries [5] and [12] slip into keigo ("ご記入いただけると幸いです", "活用させていただきます", "ご覧いただけます"), which breaks the plain desu/masu convention. That is more defensible in the legal notice in [12] than in the survey text in [5].

examples.source: These exams on the IBM Training site may be temporarily unavailable
examples.translation: IBM TrainingサイトのこれらのAの試験は
examples.suggested: IBM Trainingサイトのこれらの試験は
examples.why: A stray 'A' (probably a typo or tokenization artifact) makes the phrase read as garbled.

examples.source: Please take a moment to help us improve our course by filling out the following quick survey. Your feedback will be used to enhance...
examples.translation: 以下の簡単なアンケートにご記入いただけると幸いです。…向上に活用させていただきます。
examples.suggested: 以下の簡単なアンケートに記入してください。…向上に活用します。
examples.why: Uses keigo (いただける/させていただきます), which goes against the site's plain desu/masu register.

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed here.
examples.translation: IBMプライバシーステートメントは[こちら]からご覧いただけます。
examples.suggested: IBMプライバシーステートメントは[こちら]で確認できます。
examples.why: ご覧いただけます is a keigo form the style convention bans. It is minor here because the text is a legal notice.

editor_note: Entry 36 is faithful and reads naturally. The 0/1 settings (0は最適化なし, 1（デフォルト）は…ある程度最適化), the 0-3 alternative and the reason for setting optimization to 0 with 'skip\_transpilation = true' (すでにパスマネージャーでトランスパイル済み) all match the English, and the terms パスマネージャー and トランスパイル are consistent with the rest of the page.

The meaning is faithful throughout, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The pass threshold (16 of 20), the lock after two failed attempts ("2回の試験で合格点を取得できなかった場合…一時的にロック") and the Credly data-sharing terms all match the English. The survey paragraph [5] breaks the house register by using keigo ("ご記入いただき", "いただいた", "活用させていただきます"). The privacy notice [12] also ends in keigo ("ご覧いただけます"). Plain desu/masu would fit the rest of the site better.

examples.source: Please take a moment to help us improve our course by filling out the following quick survey. Your feedback will be used to enhance our content offering and user experience.
examples.translation: 以下の[簡単なアンケート]にご記入いただき、コースの改善にご協力ください。いただいたフィードバックは、コンテンツとユーザー体験の向上に活用させていただきます。
examples.suggested: 以下の[簡単なアンケート]に回答して、コースの改善にご協力ください。皆さんのフィードバックは、コンテンツとユーザー体験の向上に活用します。
examples.why: This uses keigo (いただく／させていただく). The house convention is polite desu/masu without keigo.

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed here.
examples.translation: IBMプライバシーステートメントは[こちら]からご覧いただけます。
examples.suggested: IBMプライバシーステートメントは[こちら]で確認できます。
examples.why: ご覧いただけます is keigo, which the register convention rules out. A legal notice makes this a small slip, not a serious one.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout: the course overview [4], prerequisites and exam/badge flow [11] match the English and nothing would mislead a learner. The Credly notice [16] has two small slips. It uses keigo ("ご覧いただけます", used twice), which breaks the page's plain desu/masu convention. It also describes Credly, a company, as "米国在住の". 在住 is used for people, so a company should be "米国に所在する".

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM and located in the United States
examples.translation: IBM が承認した米国在住のサードパーティデータ処理業者
examples.suggested: IBM が承認した、米国に所在するサードパーティのデータ処理業者
examples.why: 在住 describes where a person lives. For a company, the natural wording is 所在する or 拠点を置く.

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed [here]
examples.translation: IBM プライバシーステートメントは[こちら](...)でご覧いただけます。
examples.suggested: IBM プライバシーステートメントは[こちら](...)で確認できます。
examples.why: ご覧いただけます is keigo, which the plain desu/masu convention excludes. It appears twice in this entry.

editor_note: Entries 10 and 162 are faithful: the video title and the step labels (ステップ0–4) keep the English meaning. Entry 111 has two problems. First, it renders the italicised "$\it{some}$" (meaning any arbitrary basis) as "ある種の" (a certain kind of), which blurs the contrast with "特定の正規直交基底". Second, it drops the bold emphasis on "__not__". Also, "スケッチ証明" is a calque; a native writer would say "証明の概略". None of these misleads a learner, so the verdict is MINOR_ISSUES, not FAIL.

examples.source: the advantage of the Krylov method is __not__ related to the use of $\it{some}$ orthonormal basis, but to the use of a particular orthonormal basis
examples.translation: クリロフ法の優位性は $\it{ある種の}$ 正規直交基底を使うことではなく、…特定の正規直交基底を使うことに関係しています
examples.suggested: クリロフ法の優位性は $\it{何らかの}$ 正規直交基底を使うこと__ではなく__、…特定の正規直交基底を使うことにあります
examples.why: Here 'some' means any arbitrary basis. 'ある種の' reads as 'a certain kind of', which is close to '特定の', so the intended contrast between any basis and a particular basis gets weaker. The bold emphasis on 'not' is also dropped.

examples.source: We have already seen this from the sketch of a proof in the first section of this lesson
examples.translation: このレッスンの第1節のスケッチ証明から既にわかっていたことであり
examples.suggested: これはこのレッスンの第1節で示した証明の概略からすでに見たとおりであり
examples.why: 'スケッチ証明' is a calque of 'sketch of a proof'; the conventional Japanese phrasing is '証明の概略' or '証明のスケッチ'.

editor_note: Of the five rewritten entries, 44 (変分原理) and 47 are accurate. Entries 21, 22 and 67 need small edits, and none of them misleads a learner. Entry 22 turns "in this lesson" into この後のレッスンで ("in later lessons"). That fits entry 91, where the lesson uses only a very small Hamiltonian, but it doesn't match the English and should say このレッスンでは. Entry 21's 記述するためにスケールすることができません is a stiff calque of "cannot scale to describe", and entry 67's コスト関数の中に Estimator を使う uses the wrong particle (should be の中で).

examples.source: We will encounter Hamiltonians in this lesson much larger than that above.
examples.translation: この後のレッスンで、上記よりもはるかに大きなハミルトニアンに出会うことになります。
examples.suggested: このレッスンでは、上記よりもはるかに大きなハミルトニアンに出会うことになります。
examples.why: The English says "in this lesson", but the translation says "in later lessons". This makes little practical difference because the lesson's own example Hamiltonian is small (entry 91), so it is minor, but the text should follow the source.

examples.source: Brute force classical eigensolvers cannot scale to describe the energies or geometries of very large systems of atoms
examples.translation: …非常に大きな原子系のエネルギーや幾何学的構造を記述するためにスケールすることができません。
examples.suggested: 古典的な総当たり固有値ソルバーでは、医薬品やタンパク質のような非常に大きな原子系のエネルギーや構造を記述できるほどにはスケールしません。
examples.why: 〜するためにスケールすることができません is a word-for-word copy of the English structure. A Japanese technical writer would phrase it as 〜できるほどスケールしない or 大規模系には適用できない.

examples.source: one often sees Estimator inside a cost function
examples.translation: コスト関数の中に Estimator を使うことがよくあります。
examples.suggested: コスト関数の中で Estimator を使うことがよくあります。
examples.why: With 使う, the verb needs the particle で, not に, so 中に is ungrammatical here. 中で is the correct form.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The distinctions between 誤り抑制, 誤り軽減, 誤り検出 and 誤り訂正 are kept, and so are the caveats in [7] (it lacks full fault-tolerant structure) and [8] (パウリツイリング is noise tailoring, not strictly suppression). Entry [9] uses the keigo form ご覧ください, which breaks the plain desu/masu convention. The same entry opens two sentences in a row with 一方 ("…である一方、…。一方で、…"), which reads awkwardly. The closing line [11], 手の届くところにする, is also slightly unidiomatic.

examples.source: see [this tutorial](/tutorials/combine-error-mitigation-techniques) on IBM Quantum® Platform.
examples.translation: IBM Quantum® Platformの[このチュートリアル](...)をご覧ください。
examples.suggested: IBM Quantum® Platformの[このチュートリアル](...)を参照してください。
examples.why: ご覧ください is keigo, which the project's register convention rules out. 参照してください is plain polite form.

examples.source: Suppression and mitigation are widely applicable today, while error detection ... Meanwhile, increasingly advanced forms of error correction are steadily coming within reach.
examples.translation: 抑制と軽減は今日広く適用可能である一方、誤り検出は…使用できます。一方で、ますます高度な形の誤り訂正も…
examples.suggested: 抑制と軽減は現在すでに幅広く適用でき、誤り検出も一部のワークフローで…使用できます。さらに、より高度な誤り訂正も着実に実現に近づいています。
examples.why: Two sentences in a row built on 一方 read as a calque of 'while ... Meanwhile'. 'Meanwhile' here adds a point rather than setting up a contrast.

examples.source: Join us as we explore the tools that will help bring quantum advantage within reach.
examples.translation: 量子優位性を手の届くところにするツールを一緒に探求していきましょう。
examples.suggested: 量子優位性の実現を手の届くものにするツールを、一緒に探っていきましょう。
examples.why: 〜を手の届くところにする is an awkward collocation. 手の届くものにする, or 実現に近づける, is more idiomatic.

editor_note: Entry 145 is faithful and reads naturally: 「この2つの方程式を同時に満たす係数…は存在しません」 keeps the non-existence claim intact, 「テンソル積では表現できません」 matches the definition in [139], and it uses もつれ状態, the same term as the surrounding section.

None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 48 lists all four Qiskit-pattern steps correctly and entry 12 gets the Eagle/127-qubit/heavy-hex details and the coloring-into-parallel-layers point right. Two small fixes are still worth making. First, the heading in entry 64 now uses 事後処理 for 'Post-process', but entry 48 (rewritten the same day) uses 後処理, so the same step has two names; 後処理 should be used in both. Second, entry 12's 結合マップを**カラーリング**してレイヤーにグループ化します drops the object 'them' (the ZZ interactions), so it can be read as grouping the coupling map itself into layers.

examples.source: 5.3 Post-process
examples.translation: 5.3 事後処理
examples.suggested: 5.3 後処理
examples.why: Entry 48 renders the same Qiskit-pattern step as Post-Process（後処理）, so the rewritten heading is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: Hence, they **color the coupling map** to group them into layers.
examples.translation: そのため、彼らは結合マップを**カラーリング**してレイヤーにグループ化します。
examples.suggested: そのため、彼らは結合マップを**カラーリング**し、$ZZ$相互作用をレイヤーにグループ化します。
examples.why: Without an object, the sentence can be read as grouping the coupling map, not the ZZ interactions, into layers. Naming the object makes it clear.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The core terms are correct and used consistently: アンザッツ, 変分形式, 参照状態, エンタングルメント層, 期待値. A few spots still need an editor's touch. The variational-form tooltip in [6] says 繰り返し回数だけ繰り返される, which repeats itself and never says the layers repeat "a certain number of times". [5] uses 便利に関連付けられています, a stiff word-for-word rendering of "conveniently related". [33] drops the qualifier "typically", and [34] turns "can be important" into a flat 重要です. Both are small changes in how strong the claim is.

examples.source: Layers of parameterized gates that are repeated a certain number of times
examples.translation: 繰り返し回数だけ繰り返されるパラメータ化されたゲートの層
examples.suggested: 一定回数繰り返されるパラメータ化されたゲートの層
examples.why: The phrase repeats itself and says nothing; the English means the layers repeat a fixed number of times.

examples.source: which are conveniently related through some well-behaved mapping
examples.translation: 適切に振る舞うマッピング（例えば、連続的、微分可能）を通じて便利に関連付けられています
examples.suggested: 性質の良い写像（例えば連続かつ微分可能な写像）によって都合よく結び付けられています
examples.why: 便利に関連付けられる is a word-for-word rendering of the English; a native technical writer would use 都合よく or 性質の良い写像.

examples.source: The N-local ansatz is typically composed of simple, local gates
examples.translation: N-local アンザッツは、…シンプルなローカルゲートで構成されます。
examples.suggested: N-local アンザッツは通常、…シンプルなローカルゲートで構成されます。
examples.why: Dropping 'typically' turns a general tendency into an absolute rule.

examples.source: which can be important for simulating complex quantum systems
examples.translation: 複雑な量子システムのシミュレーションにおいて重要です
examples.suggested: 複雑な量子システムのシミュレーションにおいて重要となり得ます
examples.why: 'can be important' becomes a flat 'is important', a slightly stronger claim than the English makes.

editor_note: I judged only entry 7, the one rewritten entry. It gets the meaning right, but a native editor would still change two things. First, the hedge in "can support the development of tools" is dropped: 「ツール開発を支援します」 states the benefit as a fact. Using 「支援し得ます」 or 「役立ちます」 would keep the tentative tone. Second, the opening 「電力系統が…発電や変化する需要を統合する中で」 follows the English "integrate" too literally and reads stiffly. Neither problem would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Predicting whether operating conditions are stable can support the development of tools for managing these increasingly complex systems.
examples.translation: 運用条件が安定しているかどうかを予測することは、ますます複雑化するこれらのシステムを管理するためのツール開発を支援します。
examples.suggested: 運用条件が安定しているかどうかを予測できれば、ますます複雑化するこうしたシステムを管理するツールの開発に役立ち得ます。
examples.why: The hedge 'can' is dropped, so a possible benefit becomes a flat statement. This is a small overstatement, not a misleading one.

examples.source: as electricity systems integrate variable renewable generation and changing demand
examples.translation: 電力系統が変動する再生可能エネルギー発電や変化する需要を統合する中で
examples.suggested: 変動性の高い再生可能エネルギーの導入が進み、需要も変化する中で、電力系統の安定性を維持することは重要な課題です。
examples.why: Saying a power system 「統合する」 demand is a literal calque of 'integrate'. A Japanese technical writer would say renewables are 導入 (introduced) and that demand changes.
